The CO is then compressed, cooled, and liquefied before 2 being transferred to insulated pressure vessels for later loading onto marine tankers. Displaced CO gas from the storage units is recompressed and mixed with the incoming CO gas from the 2 2 pipeline and liquefied. Inert components that are separated from the CO in the stripper are vented into 2 the atmosphere through a vent stack, along with a small amount of CO . 2 No other continuous venting of CO is anticipated during normal operations. 2 During later project phases, control of the CO gathering network will be integrated with the T-RICH plant 2 design to ensure that the appropriate communication and control protocols are incorporated into the design of both systems. 4.7.2 NORMAL OPERATION WITH LOADING OF CO TO MARINE TANKER 2 In this mode the liquefaction plant operates as outlined above. Twice a week, CO is transferred from the storage units to the CO carrier ship for shipment across the 2 2 Gulf of Mexico to Louisiana or Texas. During this operation, liquid and vapor loading arms are connected to the liquid and vapor manifolds on the carrier ship. As necessary, the vapor lines are used to pressurize the ship’s systems before receipt of the liquid cargo. Liquid CO is pumped from the storage vessels through the metering package and 2 analyzers, to the liquid loading pipeline, liquid loading arm, and onto the ship. As the Liquid CO enters 2 the ship, displaced gas from the ship’s storage tanks is routed back to the onshore storage vessels via the vapor return loading arm, vapor return piping/pipeline, and vapor return metering package. Any CO vapor present in the loading system—such as that generated by heat entering the system during 2 operation without loading, or vapor produced when LCO contacts warm steel in the loading arm—is 2 separated from the LCO in the ship's storage tanks and is routed to the plant as outlined above. 2 Page82 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version The onsite pressure control facilities continually manage any excess CO gas from the ship, mixing it with 2 the incoming CO gas from the pipeline.
